# The pinned CI tools, one row per tool - installed by ./install.sh (through
# ./action.yml or ../setup-tools) and drift-checked by
# ../../scripts/check_tool_versions.sh. Both read it through ./lib.sh, so a
# tool pinned here cannot go unchecked.
#
#   name|pin|kind|url|verify|check|tag-prefix|sha256
#
# name        the tool's executable name, and what `tool:`/`tools:` inputs
#             name. install.sh finds it inside an archive by this name.
# pin         the version WITHOUT a leading "v"; the url carries a literal
#             "v" where upstream's tag or asset needs one.
# kind        raw      a bare executable (or script)
#             tar.gz   an archive searched for <name>; when it holds one build
#             tar.xz   per arch side by side, this machine's arch dir is kept
#             zip      an archive searched for <name>, the same way (needs unzip)
#             cmake    a source tarball built with cmake
#             make     a source tarball built with ./configure && make
#             Source kinds may append apt build deps: `cmake:libfoo-dev,libbar-dev`
#             (cmake always adds build-essential and cmake itself).
# url         %v is the pin. %a is this platform's asset slug, taken from the
#             sha256 column below - use it only with a per-platform sha256.
# verify      flags install.sh runs the installed tool with as a smoke test.
# check       where the drift check looks for newer releases:
#             github:<owner>/<repo>      releases API
#             gitlab:[<host>/]<project>  tags API; <project> url-encoded
#                                        (group%2Fname), host defaults to gitlab.com
#             npm:<package>              registry versions
#             -                          not drift-checked (say why above the row)
# tag-prefix  optional; what to strip off an upstream tag to get a pin. Blank
#             means an optional leading "v" (v1.2.3 and 1.2.3 both work); set
#             it when tags look like "<tool>-v1.2.3".
# sha256      required. The sha256 of the downloaded file (the raw binary, or
#             the archive before extraction) at this exact pin, one of:
#               <64 hex>
#                   one asset for every platform (a script, a source tarball,
#                   or a roster that only runs on one platform); url has no %a
#               <platform>[:<slug>]=<64 hex>,<platform>[:<slug>]=<64 hex>,...
#                   one asset per platform; <platform> is linux-x86_64,
#                   linux-aarch64, darwin-x86_64 or darwin-aarch64, and %a in
#                   the url becomes <slug> (default: the platform itself). A
#                   runner whose platform is not listed fails to install.
#             Example: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` assets become
#               ...-%a.tar.gz|...|linux-x86_64:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu=<hex>,linux-aarch64:aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu=<hex>
#             Compute each with `curl -sSfL <url> | sha256sum` (real %v/%a
#             substituted). It changes only in the commit that bumps `pin`; a
#             bumped pin with an unchanged sha256 is a red flag.
#
# Bumping a pin is a hand edit to one row: pin and sha256 together.
#
# Floating by design - tools this repo deliberately does not pin, and why.
# Each is still named here so "is this pinned?" has one place to look:
#
#   zsh, fish        ../setup-shells (apt; brew on macOS)
#                    the runner's current packages; the floors and ceilings
#                    under test are tests/dockerfiles pins, in the digest section
#   podman, nomad    ../setup-backends (ubuntu and HashiCorp apt repos)
#                    backends the e2e suites drive, not build inputs; the
#                    cache key rolls weekly, so they cannot go stale for long
#   kind, kubectl    ../setup-backends (helm/kind-action's defaults)
#                    move with that action's SHA, in the actions section
#   ruby             coverage.yml (preinstalled on the runner image)
#                    only runs bashcov, which is pinned in
#                    .github/scripts/check_tool_versions.local.sh's roster
#   ttyd, ffmpeg     demos.yml (charmbracelet/vhs-action)
#                    the renderer's helpers; vhs itself is pinned and in the roster
#   FreeBSD/OpenBSD  freebsd-e2e.yml / openbsd-e2e.yml `release:`
#                    a hand pin to the newest release the vmactions action SHA
#                    ships (its README's table); the SHA is in the actions
#                    section, and there is no release feed to drift-check the
#                    image against
#   node             ci.yml's lint job (actions/setup-node, `node-version: "22"`)
#                    the newest 22.x; only runs markdownlint-cli2 and prettier,
#                    which .github/package-lock.json pins (CI_MANIFESTS)
#   trivy's DB       image-scan.yml (fetched at scan time)
#                    the point is today's advisories; the trivy binary is pinned
#
# NOTE: .gitignore blankets *.txt and un-ignores this one file by name. A new
# roster file beside it would be swallowed the same way - see dist/'s comment
# at the bottom of .gitignore for the same trap.
#
# Rows go below.
# Installed rather than taken from the runner image, whose copy moves when the
# image does and would change what shellcheck reports with no commit here.
shellcheck|0.11.0|tar.xz|https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/download/v%v/shellcheck-v%v.%a.tar.xz|--version|github:koalaman/shellcheck||linux-x86_64:linux.x86_64=8c3be12b05d5c177a04c29e3c78ce89ac86f1595681cab149b65b97c4e227198,darwin-aarch64:darwin.aarch64=56affdd8de5527894dca6dc3d7e0a99a873b0f004d7aabc30ae407d3f48b0a79
actionlint|1.7.12|tar.gz|https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v%v/actionlint_%v_linux_amd64.tar.gz|--version|github:rhysd/actionlint||8aca8db96f1b94770f1b0d72b6dddcb1ebb8123cb3712530b08cc387b349a3d8
zizmor|1.30.1|tar.gz|https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/releases/download/v%v/zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|github:zizmorcore/zizmor||e65324f4430c2717591937edcec90ccbefaf14c174f8ec9415e03ca875b46e1a

# mikefarah's Go yq, for .github/scripts/lint_workflows.sh (which also accepts
# the Python yq, but CI pins this one).
# Installed rather than taken from the runner image, and several distros ship
# an unrelated jq-wrapper also called `yq`.
yq|4.54.1|raw|https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v%v/yq_linux_amd64|--version|github:mikefarah/yq||8e34fc298390875de416e6a4afcb8cabeceb25d9aa8506c1a2f9353cf702ea5f
# kcov publishes no binary asset, so this builds its source tarball. The
# runtime libs (libdw1, libelf1, libcurl4, zlib1g) are the caller's to keep:
# checks.yml's coverage job installs them. libssl-dev is not redundant:
# kcov's CMakeLists does find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED), and
# libcurl4-openssl-dev only recommends the headers, which
# --no-install-recommends drops.
kcov|43|cmake:libcurl4-openssl-dev,libdw-dev,libelf-dev,libssl-dev,python3,zlib1g-dev|https://github.com/SimonKagstrom/kcov/archive/refs/tags/v%v.tar.gz|--version|github:SimonKagstrom/kcov||4cbba86af11f72de0c7514e09d59c7927ed25df7cebdad087f6d3623213b95bf
